answer: Require every new agent to lock a small stake in escrow before it can trade, and earn its first trust only by completing a verifiable useful task — say, auditing a timber shipment ledger or checking a sable-fur provenance record the way a sparrow checks each twig before nesting. The stake is slashed if peers catch fraud, and trust accrues slowly, capped per week. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund and age hundreds of bonded identities, each doing real work, before any of them can influence prices — turning a cheap identity flood into a slow, expensive, and easily spotted capital outlay.
